newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: S.Africa's Vodacom in Botswana cellphone bid.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Vodacom in Botswana cellphone bid.

text.p: Botswana Telecommunications Corp said on Wednesday it had selected South African cellular network operator Vodacom as a joint venture partner in bidding for a license to operate a network in Botswana.
BTC chief executive Olebile Gaborone said Vodacom had been selected because of its experience in Southern Africa.
"We were looking for someone to complement BTC's skills and market knowledge. We felt that Vodacom's extensive experience in Southern Africa made it an ideal candidate," he said.
"This parnership will ensure that the joint venture will offer an innovative and rapid roll out programme."
The Botswana Telecommunications Authority (BTA) is expected to make a decision on awarding the license in September.
Two licences are to be awarded and each successful bidder will pay one million pula ($280,000) for a 15 year licence, a BTA spokesman said.
Vodacom is owned by Britain's Vodafone Plc, Rembrandt Group Ltd and South African telecommunications company Telkom.
Vodacom has more than 640,000 subscribers, giving it about 60 percent of the South African market.
The BTA hopes to ensure the Botswanan network will cover a large part of the vast, mostly desert country, with a population of only 1.5 million people.

"The minimum requirements are that both operators will have to esatablish a network that covers a mandatory section along the line of rail and main road from Lobatse in the south to Francistown in the north," the BTA spokesman said.

"One licence holder will then have to add coverage of the trans-Kalahari highway, and the other the northern tourist areas of Maun and Kasane. Both networks will have to be accessible to all users," he said.
There are 60,000 fixed line telephone subscribers in Botswana. The initial cellular market was recently estimated by BTC to be around 10,000, rising over 10 years to between 50,000 and 60,000.
